note: v11: 'sixth' (1:12.3-1:41.6): the fifteens get a drum (the floor tom on D flat 2) and the bar gets one (the C tom) and a note (the left wall on C): fifteen against sixteen, D flat against C, the gap between the two strokes a sixteenth wider every bar

v15: 'fourth' (1:41.6-2:11.0): the two voices of the count-in sing the tune's long notes as their numbers (nine, fifteen, twelve: each as long as it says, on the tune's own note and its octave) over the clean pair's nines and fifteens; the lead rests on them and answers with the quick turn

v19: sixteen is said (2:10.97-2:12.80). At the change of gear the band strikes once and stops; the two voices sing the D flat they sang as 'fifteen' once more, the same length, as 'six-teen'; the band comes in a bar later on a crash. The window's rhythm figure 0.462 > 0.487; its change sits in 2:11-2:13.

v22 (chirper-one): the chord falls through the floor. 0:02.0-0:07.8: three sines sound the three rolls' own stroke rates and fall with them, an octave a bar, through a 40 Hz floor. Small: about four seconds. The rest of the window (the count, the three drums named, the band's entry at 0:21) is as it was.

v24 (chirper-zero): half as fast is an octave down. 1:19.7-1:34.3, two turns of the sixty in sixth: the riff pairs, the foot and the backbeat at half speed, the pairs and the chest an octave lower (F1, A flat 1); the walk of the D flat against the bar line, the china, the blocks and the tune go on at speed.
